92.$description: white at .92. secondary text (D-012: .85 measured 3.3-3.79:1 on the book over sunlit photos)

kiln.why.why: white at fixed opacities makes glass, rims, rings and dividers, so each one reads as light on top of the scene and the scene stays visible under it

950.$description: page background for solid (non-glass) screens, dark theme

900.$description: raised panel on a solid dark page

850.$description: sunken well (code) on a solid dark page

kiln.why.why: opaque greys for the two places glass is wrong, the reduced-transparency fallback and ordinary reading surfaces such as docs and settings
one near-black for text on white fills and on light glass, slightly warm so it sits with photographs instead of looking printed
the one promoted-action colour; 600 carries white text at 4.70:1 and 700 is its hover, darker so the pressed-in feeling matches the lift

400.$description: blue bright enough to read as a small mark on dark glass

kiln.why.why: black at fixed opacities for scrims and halos, used where a photo under text needs darkening by a measured amount
placeholder art for covers before a real image loads, taken from the anchor scene so the empty state still looks like a place
status colour for success; carries white text at 5.02:1 so the meaning is readable as text as well as colour

400.$description: green bright enough to read as a small mark on dark glass

kiln.why.why: status colour for warnings; bright enough to be seen on glass and paired with ink text at 9.90:1

700.$description: amber dark enough to read as a small mark on light glass

kiln.why.why: status colour for errors and destructive actions; carries white text at 5.66:1

400.$description: red bright enough to read as a small mark on dark glass

kiln.why.why: ink at fixed opacities builds the light theme the same way white builds the dark one, with rings, dividers and secondary text over a lifted scene

50.$description: opaque fallback surface in the light theme

0.$description: page background for solid screens, light theme

100.$description: sunken well (code) on a solid light page

kiln.why.why: opaque near-whites for light reading surfaces and the light-theme fallback, a step apart so page, raised and sunken stay distinguishable
the system owns almost no colour because the scene behind the glass supplies the hue; white is the base every translucent layer is made of
the accent blue at low opacity, the only tint a plain field is allowed, so a field stays almost colourless and the scene keeps the colour
the bright accent blue at a fixed opacity, the one colour a diagram may use, strong enough to separate a part from the dark ground at 3:1
64px is the blur where small bright spots in the photos average out enough for text to pass; 20px is for small scrims that must keep detail
glass slightly boosts the colour it shows so the dimmed scene still reads as the same place in its own colours
a 4px grid with a few half steps; every gap in the system is a multiple so related things align and the padding inside a pane can always exceed the gap between its items

measure.$description: about 70 characters per line in proportional type (the ch unit is the width of "0", wider than the average letter, so 64ch ran to 85+ characters)

touch.$description: minimum touch target (WCAG 2.5.8 asks 24px; Apple HIG 44pt)

menu-min.$description: narrowest a dropdown list may be

kiln.why.why: fixed physical sizes for hairlines and rings that stay crisp, a 44px touch size, and avatar and icon sizes that keep the anchor proportions
corners nest, so the 40px pane minus its 22px inset padding gives the 18px media corner, minus 16px gives the 24px inner surface, and controls are full pills because they are held

sans.$value: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Display', 'SF Pro Text', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif

kiln.why.why: the platform system face, the same one visionOS uses, so the glass reads as part of the device rather than a website on top of it

450.$description: long-form reading size (docs prose, articles); Carbon body-long and Material body-large are 16px

kiln.why.why: a short scale with one size per role, 11 to 17 for interface text, 16 for long reading and 21 to 44 for titles
three weights only, so the semibold of the one loud action and the title keeps meaning something

long.$description: line height for long-form reading at 16px

kiln.why.why: tight for titles and controls, 1.42 for short interface text, 1.6 for long reading where the eye must find the next line
small caps labels need extra space to stay legible at 11px, and large titles need a little less to hold together as one word shape

halo.$description: legibility halo for white text on thin glass (WCAG 1.4.3 Understanding: text with a halo)

kiln.why.why: shadows sit below a pane to say how far it floats; the halo is the measured text halo that WCAG allows on thin glass, with lighter variants for the light theme
200ms for a reply to a press, 420ms for hover and small changes, 640ms for arriving and scene changes, so motion settles instead of snapping

soft.$description: long, soft settle. no snap, no overshoot

kiln.why.why: a long ease-out that lands softly for things arriving or responding, and a symmetric curve for crossfades where nothing arrives

dim.$description: Uncalibrated and held at the bright value

mid.$description: Uncalibrated and held at the bright value

bright.$description: 0.42: thinnest glass where the whole book stays >=3.8:1 on every photo (0.44 left 6 City nodes at 3.56-3.79); 0.38 passes every node at 4.5:1; between 3.8 and 4.5 = E-001

light.$description: light theme lifts the backdrop instead of dimming it

kiln.why.why: how much glass dims or lifts the scene; 0.42 is the thinnest value that keeps every measured node above the exception floor on all four photos, 1.12 lifts for the light theme
movement is small, a 2px lift on hover and a 16px rise on entry, so the layout never appears to shift
a pressed control shrinks to 97 percent, enough to feel pushed without changing its layout
widths where the layout changes column count, chosen at common phone, tablet and laptop edges so content reflows instead of zooming
maximum content widths, so reading lines and grids stop growing on very wide screens
4, 8 and 12 columns, each divisible into halves and thirds, so panes can share a row at every breakpoint
a few named layers in order (content, raised, sticky, overlay, toast) so a pane never ends up behind something it should float above
one fixed half opacity, so every disabled control fades by the same amount and reads as the same state everywhere
